key_insight: HiVLA separates high-level semantic planning (handled by a VLM) from low-level motor control, using visual grounding to connect them so you can preserve VLM reasoning while learning precise manipulation.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off where end-to-end fine-tuning of Vision-Language-Action models for control erodes the rich reasoning capabilities of base VLMs; enables robust, sample-efficient embodied manipulation without sacrificing semantic understanding.
method: Hierarchical architecture: a VLM-based high-level planner produces visually grounded semantic plans (tasks, parts, subgoals).
Decoupled low-level controller: separate motor policy learns precise primitives and closed-loop visual feedback for execution.
Grounding & interface module: translates VLM plans into actionable primitives and maintains alignment between vision, language, and control (VLM largely preserved or lightly adapted).
impact: Enables practitioners to leverage powerful VLM reasoning for complex manipulation while training modular controllers that are more sample-efficient, generalize better, and are easier to maintain and update.
visual_elements: Hierarchical pipeline diagram: VLM planner (semantic) → grounding module → low-level controller (motor) → robot execution
Before/after comparison chart: end-to-end fine-tune vs HiVLA showing preserved reasoning vs improved control metrics
Attention/grounding overlay on scene images: visualized parts/subgoals the VLM references
Sequence storyboard: semantic subgoal → primitive action → outcome (illustrate closed-loop feedback)
paper_title: HiVLA: A Visual-Grounded-Centric Hierarchical Embodied Manipulation System
paper_authors: Tianshuo Yang, Guanyu Chen, Yutian Chen, Zhixuan Liang, Yitian Liu
